title: Town mood and camera-composition references
scope: Owner-selected positive references for town mood, composition and the relationship between establishing and closer interaction views. Generated concept screenshots; names and interface copy are illustrative.

images.title: Lowland port — arrival
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept.
Asset type: a single polished fictional in-game screenshot for Wandering Year, an indie fantasy trekking RPG. This is a visual design exploration.
FORMAT: one complete widescreen 16:9 game view, preferably about 1920x1080. No collage, no multiple panels, no outer frame, no explanatory callouts or watermark.
ART DIRECTION: convincingly rendered fixed-camera 3D environment made of a modest, reusable kit of textured buildings and scenic props. Aged fantasy-paperback warmth translated into tangible modular game geometry: mellow ochres, sun-faded red cloth, muted teal/green painted wood and glazed ceramic accents, cooler distant landforms. Clear silhouettes, softly shaded solid volumes, restrained hand-painted texture character and simplified material response, large calm color areas. Sophisticated light and layered atmospheric depth. Serious, quietly beautiful, welcoming. Believable early-modern fantasy architecture and practical expedition culture with magic and common gunpowder, no modern machinery. Slightly eccentric curved lintels, tapered timbers and ornamental ceramic inserts suggest a distinct living culture. Occasional older curved stone remnants may be reused in recent buildings. Architecture must remain legible as modelable parts.
Avoid generic medieval castle villages, thatched fantasy cottages everywhere, Disney/storybook cuteness, anime, flat untextured low-poly facets, photo/PBR microdetail, AAA visual noise, giant glowing magical devices, full-screen pixelation and painted-paper overlays. The view must feel like a playable 3D scene, not an oil painting or aerial model village.
COMPOSITION: a composed arrival view from human height or just above it, looking INTO the inhabited space. No visible player avatar, weapon, hands, crosshair or combat HUD. Clear foreground depth elements, middle-distance service buildings and a geographically meaningful background. Three or four readable destinations; other buildings are quiet supporting shapes. Do not crowd every surface with props. Small distant people only, natural adult proportions, no large foreground character. Warmth comes from shelter, ongoing ordinary life, light, a visible place to eat/rest and human company.
UI: minimal coherent RPG interface, thin warm bronze dividers on dark translucent desaturated teal/charcoal panels, cream legible restrained serif text. A small location title at upper left. A very shallow compact service/navigation strip at the bottom occupying at most 7% of the picture. One small hover label near a welcoming doorway and a discreet pointer. No minimap, stat meters, quest markers, city-management dashboard, modal overlay, ornate filigree or large title logo. Use only the exact text specified per scene.
SCENE: a prosperous but human-scale river-mouth port after a brief spring shower, soft bright afternoon sun and a clearing blue-green sky. View from the shelter of a sailcloth canopy at the edge of a quay: the canopy corner and two weathered timber uprights make close foreground depth; a low stone quay leads diagonally into a broad convivial square. Left/middle, an inviting two-storey inn with ochre limewash, a muted teal projecting upper gallery, wide curved lintel and an open door. Opposite, a cloth-awning provisioner and a practical boatwright/sail loft; a shared architectural kit is apparent. Small hanging laundry, restrained baskets and a couple of cargo bundles. Beyond the right side a slow estuary with moored river craft, a few distant masts and layered lush low hills; no vast fleet. A distinctive broad ancient stone arch reused as a quay support gives this port an identity without making it a ruin. Four tiny people chatting or carrying ordinary bundles. Thin chimney smoke, damp matte paving with a few softly reflective puddles; no mirror-polished streets. The place feels prosperous, friendly, unhurried and easy to read, with a visible clear route to the inn.
TEXT exactly: location "Salt Reach"; hover label "The Lantern House"; bottom controls "Inn" "Provisions" "Boatwright" "Depart".
Show plenty of daylight and local material color. Shelter and human company must communicate welcome without depending on everything glowing orange.

SCENE: a small upriver town on a cold rainy late afternoon. View from under a deep timber overhang on a landing, a wet post and the overhang corner in the immediate foreground. Three substantial service facades stand across a short sheltered lane: central inn, a provisioner under a sun-faded red awning, and a small boat repair shed beside the river. One legible old curved stone bridge crosses behind the square towards dark green wooded slopes, wet rock and mist in the valley. Buildings share ochre plaster, restrained teal joinery and ceramic lintel details with the lowland culture, but have steeper practical roofs and more timber. Compose a human-scale refuge, not a dense city or fortress. The inn's amber-lit open doorway and two windows have a warm table visible deep inside; a bench and a little stacked firewood sit under the eaves. One small silhouette hurries under a shelter and two converse in a protected corner. Rain is visible against the background and drips off the eaves; foreground shelter looks dry. A little smoke and gently wind-shaped cloth imply ambient motion. Warmth is concentrated in hospitable openings; the whole scene stays readable in softened blue-green daylight rather than being a dark horror image.
TEXT exactly: location "Alder Ferry"; hover label "The Hearth"; bottom controls "Inn" "Provisions" "Landing" "Depart".
The core feeling is relief after a wet trek, a place to put down a pack and find food and conversation. Leave a quiet lower portion of the view useful for a later dialogue overlay.

SCENE: a small inhabited waystation just below the dry high mountains, at clear, cold early evening. This is a rare refuge far upriver, not the starting town. A sheltered courtyard is bounded by three sturdy ochre-stone buildings with timber galleries, low heavy roofs, muted teal shutters and sun-faded red wind curtains. Keep the architectural family of curved lintels and ceramic inserts, adapted to local rock. The court and inn entrance are close and readable. A waist-high stone wind wall and the underside of a porch frame the foreground. An immense dry sculpted mountain ridge, pale striated cliffs and remote snowy peaks rise beyond one open side; layered cool distances make the town feel tiny in a big world. A narrow watercourse or modest stone cistern quietly connects it to an upriver route. Restrained warm light through an open common-room door, a kettle/steam silhouette inside, small sheltered lamps. Two tiny people carrying firewood together give company and scale; no adventuring combat party, no guards in plate armor. Thin smoke drifts over the roof, a red cloth edge moves gently. The stone catches the last pale sun; air is cold and clear. Atmospheric but calm, protected and welcoming.
TEXT exactly: location "Stonewell"; hover label "The Common Room"; bottom controls "Inn" "Supplies" "Guide" "Depart".
Do not make a grim fortress, forbidding castle, canyon dungeon or snowy starting pass. This is a loved ordinary place where people live, surrounded by vast severe geography.

images.title: Inn conversation — portrait interface
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup, edit of an existing fictional game screenshot.
The attached image is the exact scene to preserve: Alder Ferry, the rainy upriver town. Keep its widescreen aspect, camera, buildings, signs, lighting, weather, colors, people and top-left location title unchanged. Do not redesign or regenerate the town. We are showing a new UI state of the same fixed-camera town prototype.
Replace the bottom navigation strip and cover the lower roughly 30 percent of the image with a beautifully legible restrained classic RPG conversation interface. The whole upper 70 percent remains the same scene, bright and crisp enough that the rain, sheltered doorway and town mood remain present. Remove the floating "The Hearth" hover label while the dialogue is open.
Panel: desaturated dark teal-charcoal with a thin warm bronze border and subtle material tone, broad calm surfaces, warm ivory text, discreet hover highlight. No ornate scrollwork, mobile-app cards, modern glassmorphism, stats, quest markers or portrait speech balloon.
At the left of the lower panel, a framed rectangular painted portrait of a kindly practical woman innkeeper around fifty, natural adult proportions, weathered warm face, a few grey hairs, simple cream work shirt and muted teal shawl, looking directly at the visitor with an unforced welcome. It should read as a separate illustrated RPG portrait with restrained painted surfaces, not a close-up 3D human standing in the town, not an anime character or glamorous cosplay model. The portrait occupies about one fifth of panel width, leaving ample readable text.
To its right name text EXACTLY "Mara, innkeeper"
Dialogue text EXACTLY "You're soaked through. Come in, there's stew left."
Below it, three neatly spaced selectable responses EXACTLY:
"A meal and a bed."
"How is the river?"
"I'll stay a while."
A small separate bottom-right control EXACTLY "Back to town".
Use only this conversation text plus the unchanged town title. Strong reading hierarchy, comfortable margins, realistic game screenshot layout. A single image, no collage, no watermark or design annotations. Preserve the original environment composition and mood.

images.title: Provisioner — shop interface
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup, edit of an existing fictional game screenshot.

Keep its widescreen aspect, camera position, architecture, colors, lighting, human figures and location title unchanged. We are showing a new shop UI state over the same fixed-camera scene, not inventing a new environment. Remove the floating "The Lantern House" hover label and the bottom service navigation strip.
Keep approximately the left 58 percent of the town completely visible. Overlay a calm, readable, vertical provisioner's shop interface on the right approximately 40 percent of the screen, with good outer margins and only modest background transparency. The player should still feel present in a sunny port, with the inn and foreground canopy visible to the left.
UI materials: desaturated dark teal/charcoal, thin warm bronze dividers, warm ivory lettering, restrained classic RPG typography matching the original screenshot. Plenty of breathing room. No ornate rococo borders, mobile-app cards, stats dashboard, quest markers, modern cash-register checkout or huge backpack grid.
At panel top a small rectangular illustrated portrait of a practical middle-aged merchant with a friendly face, simple sun-faded red working waistcoat over an off-white shirt, no fantasy armor. Portrait shares the soft painted look appropriate to this world and stays secondary to supplies.
Title EXACTLY "Edda's Provisions"
Small welcome EXACTLY "Something for the road?"
Four clear item rows, each with a small readable painted object icon: a cloth-wrapped ration parcel, a ceramic oil flask, a folded wool pair of socks, a folded waxed-cloth sheet.
Text EXACTLY:
"Trail rations" with secondary text "Three days"
"Lamp oil" with secondary text "One flask"
"Dry socks" with secondary text "One pair"
"Waxed cloth" with secondary text "One sheet"

images.title: Salt Reach — from the approach
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / camera-distance study.
Edit the supplied fictional game screenshot into a genuinely farther-away view of THE SAME PLACE. Preserve its architectural identity, material treatment, color palette, weather, time of day and light. This is a controlled comparison of camera distance and the resulting emotional mood, not a different town design.

CAMERA CHANGE: move the camera physically backward about 50–80 metres from the original intimate scene, with only modest elevation from an approach path or bank (roughly 5–8 metres above the town's ground). Retain a natural forward-facing perspective with a visible horizon. No aerial/bird's-eye/isometric/city-management view. Reconstruct the scene from this new viewpoint; do not simply shrink the original screenshot inside a border or widen the lens from under the same porch.
The whole small group of town buildings is now visible in the middle distance, with the main inn about one quarter of the image height or less. The inhabited cluster should occupy roughly half to two thirds of the image width. Include substantial open approach and surrounding landscape. The viewer is outside the town, looking toward it; no nearby awning, porch ceiling, lamp, giant foreground barrel or embracing architectural frame. The original sheltered arrival spot can be a SMALL element within the town.
Keep the original distinctive inn, neighboring services, roof forms, joinery, banners, landmark and geography recognizable. A few necessary side/rear buildings can complete the visible cluster, but do not turn it into a huge city or invent a castle. Tiny people now give only scale and activity. Windows and doorways still contain the same warm light but their interiors and faces are no longer readable. Let the pullback reduce intimacy naturally; do not compensate by increasing brightness, adding lanterns everywhere, enlarging the buildings or changing the weather.
Maintain the original convincing textured 3D game-environment look, clear solid forms and atmosphere. Same widescreen aspect, one complete screenshot, no diptych, callouts, zoom arrows, camera schematic, outer border or watermark. Keep the small location title at upper left and the shallow bottom navigation at the original on-screen text size, independent of world camera distance. A single discreet hover label can still identify the inn; do not add map markers or management UI.

MATCH THIS SPECIFIC SCENE: Salt Reach in clear soft afternoon daylight after rain. Move to an open coastal approach path across a shallow inlet, looking at the entire small waterfront service cluster. The ochre inn with teal timber balcony, the red-awning provisioner, the white sailcloth boatyard and the old broad stone quay arch remain recognizable together. See more estuary water, curving shore and lush distant lowland hills. An unroofed stretch of path and low grasses occupy the foreground; a modest footbridge or quay connection leads into the town. Preserve a human-scale prosperous place, a few masts and the original distant hillside settlement without making the primary town sprawl everywhere.
Exact UI: "Salt Reach"; inn hover "The Lantern House"; bottom "Inn" "Provisions" "Boatwright" "Depart".
The image should test whether a welcoming town at a short distance feels like a destination being anticipated instead of immediate company.
